motivation: An exchangeability hazard test can be significant even when all breeding pairs follow the same per-capita demographic process, because a small colony has a mechanically higher probability of reaching zero. This test asks whether durable-extinction identities are more biased toward small colonies than that neutral size arithmetic predicts.
endpoint: Use the identical primary durable-extinction events, censoring, risk sets and standardized prior-size contrast frozen in PALMER_COLONY_EXTINCTION_HAZARD_V1.

neutral_model.name: island-year proportional Poisson branching
neutral_model.prior_count: n_i = breeding pairs in colony i at t-1
neutral_model.shared_growth_multiplier: r = sum_i N_i,t / sum_i n_i over analyzable previously-positive colonies in the same island-year risk set
neutral_model.one_step_count_model: N_i,t ~ Poisson(r * n_i), independently across colony codes
neutral_model.reason: This preserves a common expected per-pair demographic multiplier within each island-year while allowing smaller groups to reach zero more often purely by demographic arithmetic.

conditional_identity_null.conditioning: Condition on the observed number m of durable-extinction events in each event-bearing risk set.
conditional_identity_null.subset_weight: Under independent Bernoulli zero indicators with probabilities q_i, the conditional probability of an m-colony event subset is proportional to the product over selected colonies of q_i/(1-q_i).
conditional_identity_null.implementation: Enumerate all size-m subsets when feasible and sample from normalized log-weights; fail closed on numerical degeneracy.
conditional_identity_null.statistic: Same equal-risk-set-weighted standardized prior-size contrast as the primary exchangeability test.
conditional_identity_null.p_value: one-sided lower-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

decision_rule.mechanistic_boundary: Even support does not identify predation or social facilitation; it only rejects a shared per-capita Poisson branching explanation for the size ordering of durable extinctions.
decision_rule.if_not_supported: Describe small-group disappearance as compatible with neutral demographic arithmetic under shared island-year decline; do not use it as evidence for an Allee/social-facilitation mechanism.

sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat the weighted-null test after excluding Litchfield.
sensitivities.prior_count_ge2: Repeat after requiring prior count >= 2 pairs.
sensitivities.two_zero_endpoint: Repeat with the two-zero durable-extinction sensitivity from the hazard contract.

interpretation_boundaries: The null is a demographic benchmark, not a literal mechanistic model of Adelie recruitment, survival or dispersal.
The null conditions on observed island-year total change and therefore tests within-island size ordering rather than the regional cause of decline.
Do not call a rejection proof of predation, social facilitation, snow effects or habitat quality.
Do not modify q_i, subset weighting, statistic, seed or alpha after opening this weighted-null result.
